- Model tends to overestimate prices in early days of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends, particularly when true values dip below 70.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts often overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+ → 78+).
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated; model fails to anticipate gradual pullback after peaks, especially in 70–75 range.
- Lags in response to recent low prices; model often holds forecasts too high when true values are trending down.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven corrections (e.g., ETS cap changes).
